headline: American Express has introduced a framework that records what a customer told an AI agent to buy and checks it before the agent completes the purchase.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a safeguard for agent shopping from a major card network, but it is the company's own proposal and no adoption by others is reported.
importance_line: Card holders who let an AI agent shop for them get a safeguard against it buying the wrong thing, and merchants and payment firms get a record for disputes, but it is Amex's own proposal that it hopes others will adopt, and Amex says it has seen no rise in disputes so far.
summary: TechCrunch reports, from an interview with Hannah Bozian, vice president of agentic partnerships and strategy at American Express, that Amex is introducing an Intent Intelligence Framework in which a customer's purchase instructions, such as merchant and maximum budget, are recorded and signed off before an AI agent buys, and the agent then pays with a secure payment credential instead of the real card number. Amex says the system could, for example, stop a purchase of Adidas shoes when the customer asked for white Nike sneakers, and it hopes the framework becomes an industry standard.
